subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add `first-progress` and `startup-failed` as core lifecycle phases for sub-agent startup, or solve startup silence through a narrower internal recovery/diagnostic path?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but the proposed fix creates a new core lifecycle/API surface that current consumers do not understand and the existing PR candidate is stale against current main.

options.title: Adopt additive lifecycle phases
options.body: Accept the event contract and replace the stale PR with a current-main implementation across embedded-agent, gateway, session projection, SDK, docs, and tests.

options.title: Use internal diagnostics only
options.body: Keep public lifecycle phases unchanged and instead add internal startup-failure detection, recovery, logging, and user-visible diagnostics for aborted silent starts.

options.title: Defer until broader lifecycle redesign
options.body: Leave the issue open as a product/API design item and avoid partial fixes that would add another temporary lifecycle shape.

recommendation.title: Adopt additive lifecycle phases
recommendation.body: Accept the event contract and replace the stale PR with a current-main implementation across embedded-agent, gateway, session projection, SDK, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is prior subagent lifecycle/refactor work plus current blame on the affected lifecycle projection files.
